clarification_questions.question: What does the liquid look like at the intended measurement point?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: Which method is recommended first (Clear liquid: primary method → NIR; adds UV-Vis transmission or transflection probe to the shortlist; Turbid or cloudy: adds risk: a turbid or changing liquid (probe geometries to compare); Opaque, such as milky or dense: adds UV-Vis ATR probe to the shortlist; drops NIR transmission or transflection probe from the shortlist)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The optical character decides between transmission, transflection and reflection or ATR geometries.

clarification_questions.question: Which industry or application area is this liquid process used in?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: Which method is recommended first (Dairy or food: primary method → NIR; adds NIR diffuse reflection probe to the shortlist; Bioprocess or fermentation: primary method → NIR; adds UV-Vis ATR probe to the shortlist)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Published applications of the same area weigh most when the methods are ranked.

clarification_questions.question: Is the measurement intended for research, a pilot line or production?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Research or development: plan: a screening-level plan is enough; Pilot or trial line: plan: validation at pilot scale; Production, monitoring or batch release: plan: stricter validation plan)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The intended use sets how strict the validation plan has to be.

clarification_questions.question: Is there a reference method that provides comparison values for the liquid?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Yes, a laboratory method: plan: calibrate against it and state its own error; No, none yet: plan: a reference measurement campaign comes first)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Models can only be as good as the reference values they are built on.

clarification_questions.question: Do you already have numerical acceptance criteria, such as required accuracy or a detection limit?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Yes, they are defined: plan: test against the agreed criteria; Not yet: plan: agree numerical criteria before the test)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Without them the experiment has no go or no-go criterion.

clarification_questions.question: Once the target variable is defined, over what range must it be monitored?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Narrow, around a set point: plan: sample around the set point; Wide, from low to high: plan: sample the full range)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The range decides whether the sensitivity of a method can be enough.

rationale.text: Testing several optical methods supports method selection when sample composition is incompletely known.
As the first experiment, compare MIR, NIR and Raman on retained representative good and off-specification samples before choosing a method.

limitations.text: Overlapping NIR bands suggest the use of chemometrics for quantitative and qualitative analysis of spectral data.
Fluorescence background can overwhelm the Raman signal of many organic compounds.

risk.text: Whether retained samples preserve the process differences is unknown.

risks.mitigation: Confirm sample integrity with the client

feasibility_plan.objective: Test whether spectral differences between good and off-specification samples can be linked to a defined quality variable.
clarify_first: What does the liquid look like at the measurement point?
Which industry or application area is this for?

samples_and_states.text: Collect representative retained good and off-specification samples covering the relevant process states.

reference_measurements.text: Link each sample to its documented specification status and, once the target is defined, independent reference values.

setup.text: Record MIR, NIR and Raman spectra from the same retained samples under documented measurement conditions.

comparison.text: Compare the screening methods against documented sample status and any established target reference values.

validation.text: Validate any resulting relationship to the defined target on independent material excluded from screening and model development.

go_no_go.text: Defer method and sensor selection unless a target is defined and independent validation meets criteria agreed with you before testing.

not_demonstrated.text: Do not treat screening separation alone as proof of contaminant identity or in-line performance.

steps: Clarify appearance, application, intended use, references, criteria and target range.
Collect representative retained good and off-specification samples.
Establish sample status and independent target reference values.
Record and compare spectra under documented conditions.
Validate on independent material against pre-agreed criteria.
Proceed or stop according to validation and target definition.

decision_basis.text: Base any later method and sensor selection on comparison against independent reference values on independent material, using criteria agreed with you before testing.
